## Summary

Two-layer capture. The **quoted Aug-13 tweet is the payload**: the full rules of a previously-teased strategy, given away free — *sell one SPX put credit spread per week at the Multi-Day Saty ATR -1 level*. Self-reported backtest: 326 trades since May 2020, 95.4% win rate, profit factor 2.48, +$53,328 on a single contract, max drawdown $4,605, zero losing years, 2026 is 32-for-32. Chart (OCR'd, milkmantrades.com): cumulative P&L per 1-lot May 2020–Aug 2026 with the 15 losing weeks as red dots; **fills modeled at quote midpoint less $2.64/spread**. The **new Nov-7 tweet** is the scorecard ask: he prompts @grok to compute wins vs losses, premium collected, total loss, and profit factor *since his initial share* — i.e., holding the strategy up to an independent (LLM-computed) forward window.

## Why it matters

- **This is the strategy behind the vault's existing Milk Man ATR thread.** Weekly ATR-level short puts are exactly the pattern captured in [[2026-10-18-milk-man-atr-put-mispricing]] (the edge claim there: tail-probability mispricing) and the forward-test discipline of [[2026-10-01-milk-man-options-algo-forward-test]]. The Aug-13 reveal adds the concrete rule set the earlier notes lacked: one spread/week, SPX, short strike at Multi-Day Saty ATR -1.
- **The Grok ask is a self-audit pattern worth copying.** Asking a third party (even an LLM with data access) to score your strategy *since publication* is a cheap forward-test integrity check — separating "backtest was lucky" from "edge persisted out of sample." Bookmarks (240 on the ask, 8.6k on the reveal) say people save these as recipes.
- **Cost realism is modeled, not ignored.** The $2.64/spread haircut on midpoint fills is a real-world execution assumption many retail backtests skip — consistent with the cost-stress discipline already queued for our own harness (Inbox: cost-stress + execution-lag grid).
- **Skepticism gates:** self-reported backtest, no curve of the forward window yet (the Grok answer isn't in the captured data); 95.4% win rate on credit spreads implies high negative skew — the 15 red dots carry the entire risk story, and max DD $4,605 vs +$53k cumulative means the strategy is one bad tail from giving back a chunk. "Multi-Day Saty ATR" level definition is not fully specified in-tweet (likely from his paid/original work); replication needs the exact ATR lookback and strike-selection rule. Same regime caveat as prior captures: May 2020–Aug 2026 was mostly a favorable vol regime for short premium.
